title: Eikö … ole with plural owners
focus: Add the question ending -kö to ei: ei + -kö = eikö. Negative possession questions keep ole after the owner: Eikö sinulla ole palloa?
targetSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions

exercises.prompt: Repair “Eivätkö heillä ole peliä?” to mean “Don’t they have a game?” Use heillä ("they as owner") and peliä ("game").
exercises.explanation: Keep fixed eikö and ole; neither changes to agree with the possessor.
requiredSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
exercises.targetSkill: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.Eikö heillä ole peliä?: Keep fixed eikö and ole; neither changes to agree with the possessor.
optionFeedback.Eivätkö heillä ole peliä?: This repeats the supplied error. Keep fixed eikö and ole; neither changes to agree with the possessor.
optionFeedback.Eikö heillä on peliä?: This leaves the required noun or question pattern. Keep fixed eikö and ole; neither changes to agree with the possessor.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: he has the learned possession form heillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
peli + -ä = peliä. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.
